paragraphs.text: dsh-sieve: context engineering & token optimization plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) — tool output
filtering, context pruning, progressive skill disclosure. 36% smaller payload in offline replay. DSH
上下文管理与 token 优化节省插件。
English | 简体中文
sieve / dsh-sieve
**Your agent navigates countless decisions across long loops, yet most tokens pay for dead logs and

stale history.
sieve is a precision mesh inside the execution loop: cutting through context inflatio
n and delivering only the critical context that decides the next step.**
Context engineering, token efficiency and long-task supervision plugins for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)
**−36%** request payload (offline replay, 100 trajectories) · **−21%** main model input tokens (live
model, 80 runs) · **~0.3 s** per judgment · **0** DSH core patches
How each number was measured, and what it does not show: offline replay · live model results. The li
ve runs predate the current Jev / Laya setup.
A real session in DSH Web: while the agent reads code and runs tests, the Sieve page on the right co
unts up the estimated input token reduction and the characters taken out of the context.
sieve is a high-performance DSH plugin that filters tool output, forgets stale context, and disclose
s skills strictly on demand. Every raw output is archived before rewriting and remains one `read` aw
ay. Powered by the same judge engine, a suite of harness modules supervises long tasks to eliminate
false completions and infinite loops.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> sieve needs a judge model: **Jev** (hosted, needs an API key) or **Laya** (local, m
acOS on Apple Silicon). It never borrows the session's own model. Without one, the token-saving deci
sions change nothing and the harness modules run on their rules alone. Set one up.
## Why sieve
Your agent navigates hundreds of critical decisions across complex tool-calling loops.
Yet one glance at its real context ledger reveals a grim reality: actual user prompts and core code
represent only a tiny fraction of the payload. The overwhelming bulk is pure context inflation:
- **The tool output tsunami**: A test runner spews 8,000 characters. The model only needs the single

failing assertion, yet repeatedly pays for 200+ lines of passing tests on every subsequent turn.
-
**Ghostly stale history**: A file read thirty steps ago—long since superseded—rides along as a ghost

passenger in every request.
- **Bloated skill catalogs**: Hundreds of skill descriptions loaded at
session start when 97% are never touched, permanently diluting the model's attention.
This is not pocket change—it is a critical signal-to-noise crisis.
Input tokens snowball quadratically with every turn. As the context window chokes on dead logs, the
model's attention dilutes, hallucinations increase, and tasks stall out.
**sieve is the precision mesh built for this storm.**
No blunt truncations. Zero patches to DSH core. Before tool results enter the session and before his
tory piles into dead weight, sieve queries a lightweight judge model (~0.3 s) to prune the noise, ar
chive the byte-exact original to disk, and hand the model only lean, high-signal context.
### What it looks like
A 263-line vitest run with one failure (8,020 characters), through sieve's test-log rules:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The model receives 1,138 characters instead of 8,020 (**an 86% reduction**).
- **Byte-exact preservation**: Kept lines match the original byte for byte; failure traces, diffs, a

nd test summaries are strictly protected.
- **Zero data loss**: The full output is archived to spill

disk first—one `read` away if the agent ever needs it.
- **Cache-friendly by design**: Pruning happ
ens before the result enters the session, so prompt cache prefixes never see the bloated version.
### Why a dedicated judge model
- **The limit of static heuristics**: Regex and rule-based scripts choke on unfamiliar formats, forc

ing them to let bloated logs through untouched.
- **The cost of asking the main model**: Having the
primary LLM decide what to discard wastes expensive tokens and burns an entire reasoning turn on rou
ecide what to discard wastes expensive tokens and burns an entire reasoning turn on routine cleanup.

**sieve's approach: a dedicated sidecar judge.**
It poses lightweight, structured yes/no or single-c

hoice questions with calibrated probabilities in **~0.3 seconds** (median, offline replay).
If confi
dence falls below threshold—or if any error or timeout occurs—sieve triggers safe fallback: **the fu
ll original is kept untouched**.
## Core capabilities and use cases
For AI coding agents on DeepSeek Harness, especially with verbose test logs, frequent tool calls, lo
ng sessions or large skill catalogs.
| Area | How sieve handles it |
| **Input token reduction** | Filters redundant tool content before it enters the session, reducing

input resent on later steps |
| **Tool output filtering** | Handles build logs, test reports and com

mand output by category, protecting failure details and test summaries |
| **Context compaction / pr
uning** | Replaces irrelevant older tool results in batches, retaining archive pointers for on-deman

d retrieval |
| **Progressive skill disclosure** | Shows skills by task relevance, reducing context

window usage from unrelated descriptions |
| **Prompt cache awareness** | Processes new results befo
re they are recorded and batches historical pruning to control prefix rebuild frequency |
## What's new in 0.4.0: harness modules

> [!NOTE]
> **Released in 0.4.0**; 0.4.1 is the same plugin and also loads on DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 and lat
er. Coming from 0.3.0, which has only the token-saving decisions? Run `dsh plugin --profile web add
dsh-sieve@0.4.1 dsh-sieve-web@0.4.1` and restart `dsh web`; see Upgrade and uninstall.
Saving tokens was only the opening act. For deep, long-horizon tasks, sieve introduces six harness m
odules driven by the exact same judge engine to prevent drift, loops, and false completions:
| Module | In one line |
| **Hive** | Ask one question, get 2–6 read-only bees on it. They post findings to a shared board, a

nd the judge decides which bee needs which finding |
